checks.name: Independent price source (Coinbase)
checks.detail: Coinbase agreed on direction in 95.7% of 94 sampled windows and 100.0% of those that finished $2.00+ from the line (under $1.00: 17/21; $1.00–2.00: 14/14; $2.00–4.00: 31/31; $4.00+: 28/28). Disagreement near the line is expected: Coinbase is one exchange, the index averages several. 6 windows had no candles.

checks.name: Runs test (is the sequence random?)
checks.detail: 17,170 runs vs 16,485 expected (z = +7.54, p = 0.000): more switches than chance: results tend to alternate. Check that it also holds out of sample.

checks.name: Does one result predict the next?
checks.detail: lag-1 correlation -0.0416 (z = -7.55). Statistically non-zero, but check its size: a correlation this small moves the next window's odds by only about 2.1 percentage points, less than fees cost.

checks.name: Hour-of-day lean holds out of sample?
checks.detail: Split at 2026-06-07. Hours that looked significant in the first half: 04:00, 18:00; still significant, same direction, in the second half: none. Correlation of hourly leans between halves: +0.25 (near zero: the hourly pattern is noise).

checks.name: Streak behaviour holds out of sample?
checks.detail: after 3 Ups the next was Up 43.7% (first half, n=1,713) vs 46.8% (second half, n=1,878); after 3 Downs the next was Up 56.6% (first half, n=1,801) vs 54.9% (second half, n=1,851). For a fade-or-follow rule to pay, the same lean must show in both halves and be larger than the ~2–3¢ per contract that spread and fees cost.

checks.name: Kalshi price edge holds out of sample?
checks.detail: No price level was clearly profitable after fees. 4 more showed a paper profit that sits inside its error band, so it could just be luck: buy No at 40–50¢: +2.4¢ ±11.3 (n=75); buy Yes at 80–90¢: +2.3¢ ±5.7 (n=114); buy No at 20–30¢: +1.8¢ ±8.0 (n=102). Most windows trade under 10¢ or over 90¢; there, recent results ran -0.7¢ to +0.2¢ per contract.

checks.name: Chance findings to expect
checks.detail: The report tests 35 hour, weekday and slot groups; at 95% confidence about 1.8 would look significant by luck alone. Found: 3. That's no more than luck would produce.
